prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: desktop Electron dashboard north-star comp, landscape 16:10
Primary request: Create exactly one high-fidelity preview UI comp for the real product “Agent Arena.” The interface must feel like an authentic 1990s demoscene module tracker fused with a competitive PC shareware battle control interface—not a modern card dashboard decorated with pixels.
Scene/backdrop: Full-frame desktop application interface on a strict edge-to-edge grid.
Subject: A fixed pixel status header above two tall contestant channel strips. Left contestant: “Codex” and “gpt-5.6-sol”. Right contestant: “Claude” and “claude-opus”. A luminous horizontal playhead crosses the current event row across both channels. Below, a full-width pattern/evidence log presents real match facts and operator actions.
Style/medium: High-fidelity desktop UI design comp; authentic 8-bit/16-bit era module tracker and shareware battle interface; dense but clear operator hierarchy; crisp integer-aligned pixels; bitmap typography.
Composition/framing: Landscape 16:10. Fixed status header at top. Two equally prominent tall vertical contestant channel strips in the upper/middle workspace. Luminous horizontal playhead spans the current event row. Full-width pattern/evidence log occupies the lower section. Strong column rhythm, row numbers, channel lanes, small status meters, and tracker-like operator controls. No floating cards.
Lighting/mood: Phosphor-screen luminosity with a focused competitive operations mood. Flat pixel shading only.
Color palette: Near-black, deep indigo steel, phosphor teal, amber, magenta, icy white.
Materials/textures: Pixel phosphor, dithered steel panels, strict grid lines, bitmap glyphs, crisp hard edges.
Text (verbatim): “Agent Arena”; “Round 2”; “Verify Attacks”; “Codex”; “gpt-5.6-sol”; “Claude”; “claude-opus”; “100 HP”; “70 HP”; “4/4 checks”; “logout-retry”; “Concurrent rotations can both commit”; “Inspect Codex”; “Inspect Claude”.
Constraints: Make all listed text legible and spelling accurate where possible. The playhead must visibly cross the current event row. Preserve a disciplined, information-dense operator hierarchy. Zero rounded cards. Use only original interface graphics.
Avoid: modern card dashboard conventions, rounded cards, fake game characters, copyrighted sprites, copyrighted logos, gradients, blur, glassmorphism, soft shadows, photorealism, watermark, decorative pixel-art mascots.
